slides.heading: Blackjack Probability
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Recursion
slides.narration: Let's solve Blackjack Probability, a medium recursion problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: The dealer draws cards valued 1-10 uniformly while below target-4; busts if above target.
Starting from a hand value, probability of busting (rounded to 3 decimals).
Memoised recursion.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. The dealer draws cards valued 1-10 uniformly while below target-4; busts if above target. Starting from a hand value, probability of busting (rounded to 3 decimals). Memoised recursion.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: The chance of busting from hand total t is the average over the ten next cards, which we memoise.
slides.narration: The chance of busting from hand total t is the average over the ten next cards, which we memoise.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Plain recursion re-explores the same hands → exponential
Memoise by hand value → O(target) states × 10 cards
Bottom-up DP works equally well
slides.narration: Plain recursion explores the same hand totals repeatedly. Memoising by hand value makes it linear in the target, times ten cards.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. If the total exceeds the target, it's a bust
2. If it reaches target minus four, stop
3. Otherwise average the ten draws
4. Memoise by total
slides.narration: Step by step. First, if the total exceeds the target, it's a bust. Second, if it reaches target minus four, stop. Third, otherwise average the ten draws. Fourth, memoise by total.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Hand 16: P(bust) = 0.500
slides.narration: With a hand of 16, average over the ten possible cards. Hands of seventeen to twenty-one stand, and anything over twenty-one busts. That gives 0.500.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Hand 15: P(bust) = 0.450
slides.narration: With a hand of 15, average over the ten possible cards. Hands of seventeen to twenty-one stand, and anything over twenty-one busts. That gives 0.450.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Bust returns one above the target, zero when the dealer would stand, otherwise the memoised average of bust over the ten next cards. The answer is rounded to three decimals.

slides.heading: Complexity
bullets: Time: O(t)
Space: O(t)
slides.narration: Time is O of t. Space is O of t.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Stand when hand ≥ target − 4
Each card 1–10 has probability 0.1
Round to 3 decimals at the end only
slides.narration: The dealer stands at target minus four or more. Round only the final answer, not intermediate values.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Explain the state: just the hand total
Follow-up: realistic deck (cards without replacement)
slides.narration: The state is only the hand total because cards are drawn with replacement. A real deck adds card counts to the state.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: The chance of busting from hand total t is the average over the ten next cards, which we memoise.
Complexity: O(t)
